name: Mardin Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Village sign language (Turkey); word stress category inapplicable; only sociolinguistic notes (Dikyuva 2008/2012, Zeshan 2010).

sources.citation: de Vos, Connie & Ulrike Zeshan. 2012. Introduction: Demographic, sociocultural, and linguistic variation across rural signing communities. In Zeshan & de Vos (eds.), Sign Languages in Village Communities, 2-24. De Gruyter Mouton / Ishara Press. (same volume; Glottolog lists it as 'grammar_sketch' for mard1245)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing on stress; comparative sociolinguistic/typological overview. Whole volume text grepped for stress/prosod/accent: no statement concerning MarSL (only hits are unrelated: Yucatec Maya SL prosody remark, 'they stress that...' in Adamorobe chapter).

sources.citation: UCLan CLOK repository search for 'Mardin Sign Language' (5 hits: Webster & Safar 2019, 2020; Zeshan & Palfreyman 2017, 2020; Sagara 2014) -- none is a description of MarSL structure
sources.note: No MarSL phonology; typology/vitality papers that mention MarSL.

sources.citation: Dikyuva, Hasan, Cesar Ernesto Escobedo Delgado, Sibaji Panda & Ulrike Zeshan. 2012. Working with village sign language communities: Deaf fieldwork researchers in professional dialogue. In Zeshan & de Vos (eds.), Sign Languages in Village Communities, 313-344. (same volume)
sources.note: Nothing; fieldwork methodology and community relations for MarSL, Chican and Alipur.

sources.citation: Dikyuva, Hasan. 2012. Mardin Sign Language: Signing in a 'deaf family'. In Ulrike Zeshan & Connie de Vos (eds.), Sign Languages in Village Communities: Anthropological and Linguistic Insights (Sign Language Typology 4), 395-399. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton / Nijmegen: Ishara Press. (open access CC BY-NC-ND via OAPEN)
sources.note: Nothing. Five-page sociolinguistic sketch (family compound, family tree, map, endangerment, contact with TID and spoken Arabic mouthings); no phonology, no prosody, no statement on stress or prominence.

sources.citation: Dikyuva, Hasan & Ulrike Zeshan. 2013. Documentation of endangered sign languages: The case of Mardin Sign Language. In Mari C. Jones & Sarah Ogilvie (eds.), Keeping Languages Alive: Documentation, Pedagogy and Revitalization, 29-41. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
